markdown_report:
The best initial direction remains a **paired temporal-sensitivity audit of the supplied GRU4Rec**, with padding-invariance verification before interpreting perturbations. Research progress is 0%; no measured results or backbone implementation were supplied.

**Starting insights.** First, existing margins measure training-pair separation. Their scale dependence prevents equating larger margins with improved HR@10. Second, feedback distinguishes recent coherent interests from broad historical relevance. This motivates temporal controls without establishing actual intent. Third, histories permit controlled comparisons. Ownership, mood, ratings and compatibility remain unknown.

**Related-work insights.** First, [Does It Look Sequential?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.12008) reports dataset-dependent shuffling effects. Its shuffle can change the latest input, so additional controls must isolate earlier context. Second, [sampled-metric research](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) limits conclusions about catalog rankings. Fixed candidates support paired comparisons, not catalog-performance claims. Third, [FActScore](https://aclanthology.org/2023.emnlp-main.741/) motivates evidence-grounded interpretation. Fourth, [GRU equations](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.GRU.html) show that zero embeddings do not neutralize recurrent padding updates. Padding correctness therefore precedes temporal interpretation.

These insights define temporal dependence, ranking reliability and grounded interpretation, supported by an implementation-validity prerequisite.

| Direction | Measurement | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|
| Implementation validity | Unpadded versus padded features/scores | Backbone correctness requires verification |
| Temporal dependence | Paired ranks and top-10 overlap | Sensitivity does not establish useful intent |
| Ranking reliability | Fixed candidates; frequency strata | Sampled ranks do not establish catalog performance |
| Grounded interpretation | Definitions; explicit unknowns | Histories cannot confirm rejection reasons |

Three atomic ideas remain. Scores are originality/potential/code difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

1. **Padding-verified temporal audit — 4/7/5.** Originality: focused controlled adaptation, although perturbations are established. Potential: tests the temporal hypothesis, although distribution shift limits interpretation. Difficulty: inference avoids retraining, although padding verification, controls and uncertainty require care. References: GRU documentation; Does It Look Sequential?
2. **Frequency-stratified ranking audit — 3/6/2.** Originality: exposes aggregate blind spots, although stratification is standard. Potential: identifies sampling-sensitive failures, although it does not correct them. Difficulty: simple counts, although sparse strata limit precision. Reference: [Hidasi and Czapp](https://hidasi.eu/assets/pdf/eval_flaws_recsys23.pdf).
3. **Evidence-tagged interpretation — 4/6/3.** Originality: adapts grounding, although the principle is established. Potential: reduces unsupported conclusions, although missing preferences remain unknowable. Difficulty: simple schema changes, although semantic verification remains challenging. Reference: FActScore.

Select idea 1 for feasibility. Verify padding invariance; compare original, last-item-only, last-preserving prefix shuffle, and matched recent/old deletions preserving the latest item. Use identical targets/candidates, deterministic perturbations, paired ranks, diagnostic HR@10, top-10 Jaccard, counts and user-bootstrap intervals. Training-prefix targets remain explicitly in-sample; use validation only through authorized host interfaces. Freeze checkpoints during each audit. A padding correction requires consistent training and predictor code, followed by retraining. Preserve category routes, adapter hooks and single-model loading. Select subsequent changes exclusively by pinned macro validation HR@10; repeated validation selection can overfit, so predeclare a small comparison set. No improvement is claimed.

idea.description: Strengthen the paired GRU4Rec temporal-sensitivity diagnostic with padding-invariance verification and controls that separate latest-item evidence, earlier order and context recency.
idea.motivation: The qualitative feedback suggests that broad historical relevance may displace recent coherent interests, while existing embedding and margin probes cannot identify temporal sensitivity. The original recent-deletion condition also removed the latest item, confounding nearby-context dependence with latest-item dependence. GRU padding updates introduce another possible confound. These controls test observable model behavior without inferring latent intent, changing the backbone family or fitting additional predictors.
idea.implementation_notes:
Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), existing metrics and ModelView interfaces. view.model remains the actual nn.Module. Keep unavailable metadata category lists empty; do not use ratings, review text, prices, stores or inferred simulator traits. Missing measurements must be null with counts and reasons, rather than zeros interpreted as healthy behavior.

First verify the supplied GRU implementation in evaluation mode using identical weights and initial states. Compare each nonempty history processed without padding against its ordinary left-padded execution, different leading-padding lengths, different batch companions, and a correctly packed or explicitly state-masked reference. Compare final features and candidate scores with declared tolerances, initially atol=1e-5 and rtol=1e-4 in float32; report maximum discrepancies and backend details. Zero item embeddings alone do not make GRU padding steps inert. Directly packing left-padded tensors is incorrect. If correction is needed, compact valid items into a prefix, right-pad internally, pack using actual lengths, unpack, and scatter per-position features back into the original left-padded layout. Handle empty histories explicitly without passing zero lengths to packing. Preserve log2feats(sequence), item_emb and predict_score(features, items). A padding correction changes model computation: update both training and the embedded predictor writer, retrain, and begin a new fixed-checkpoint audit. Do not silently patch only diagnostic execution or compare corrected inference against uncorrected inference as though it were a temporal intervention.

Use a deterministic subset of at most 200 eligible users per category, chosen by a documented stable user-ID ordering or local seed-42 sampling. Construct fallback diagnostic examples solely from user_train histories: target=history[-1], context=history[:-1], followed by the baseline context-length cap. These targets were available during fitting, so report exact user–target interaction exposure as in-sample when confirmed by the sampler, or unknown if it cannot be verified. Item exposure elsewhere in training and legitimate repeated consumption are separate facts. This fallback cannot estimate unseen-interaction generalization. Prefer validation examples only when an authorized host interface exposes their existing users, targets and pinned candidates; do not inspect hidden files, replace the evaluator, or independently reconstruct its candidate sets. Keep training-prefix and validation results separate.

Require at least four context events after truncation. Let prefix=context[:-1], latest=context[-1], and k=max(1,len(prefix)//4). Compare: original context; [latest]; a seeded shuffle of prefix followed by latest; prefix[:-k]+[latest] for recent-context deletion; and prefix[k:]+[latest] for oldest-context deletion. The shuffle preserves length, item multiplicities and latest item; the deletion conditions remove equal event counts and preserve latest. Last-item-only is a separate truncation intervention. Use five predeclared deterministic prefix-shuffle permutations per user and average their diagnostic outcomes within user; these are repeated input probes of the same checkpoint, never score fusion or multiple predictors. Record unchanged permutations, including repeated-item histories.

For the training-prefix fallback, draw 99 distinct real-item negatives excluding the user's complete training history with a local seed-42 generator, keeping the target even if repeated earlier in context. Skip and count users lacking enough eligible negatives. Reuse the same candidate IDs across every variant. Left-pad variants to the baseline maximum length. Read final features at the greatest nonzero input index, never count-1 in the left-padded layout; length-1 applies only inside compacted-prefix computation. Score through predict_score without assuming a dot-product head. Break score ties by ascending item ID and define target rank as one plus the number of candidates ordered ahead of it.

Report per-variant target rank, reciprocal rank, HR@10 and sampled-candidate top-10 Jaccard against the original. Report rank change as rank_variant-rank_original and HR change as hit_variant-hit_original. For matched deletions, report rank_recent_deleted-rank_oldest_deleted and hit_recent_deleted-hit_oldest_deleted; positive rank difference or negative hit difference indicates greater damage from deleting recent context. Preserve mean and tenth-percentile margins, negative-beats-positive rate, small-margin rate and embedding alignment as supplementary diagnostics with their original definitions and limitations. The mapped cosine statistic is directional alignment, not sufficient evidence of collapse; raw margins are scale-sensitive.

Aggregate repeated perturbations within user. Run 2,000 paired bootstrap replicates with a local seed-42 generator, sampling users with replacement separately within each category and recomputing the equal-weight four-category macro difference. Report percentile 95% intervals, category counts, skip counts and per-category effects. Missing categories make the four-category macro unavailable; never silently change its denominator. Intervals are conditional on trained checkpoints, realized candidates and perturbations; they exclude retraining, negative-sampling and repeated-search uncertainty.

Optionally measure full-catalog unseen-item top-10 overlap for the same twenty training users, five per category, required by the native simulator. Label this separately from sampled-candidate overlap and the pinned validation objective. Preserve the native unseen-item exclusion rule. No ownership, current mood, compatibility, purchase quantity or confirmed rejection reason can be inferred from overlap or temporal sensitivity.

Use model.eval(), torch.no_grad(), local random generators and finally-based restoration of model mode. Keep all four category routes and one independently trained GRU4Rec checkpoint per category. Predeclare this small diagnostic panel and any subsequent training comparison; repeated validation selection remains a source of overfitting. No additional predictor, checkpoint averaging or independently fitted popularity/transition score is introduced. Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs and 200 batches per epoch. Keep DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], single-GPU execution and artifacts beneath the trial directory. Existing predictors remain unchanged for diagnostic-only work; any architecture correction must update the predictor writer and checkpoint configuration together.
idea.pseudocode:
class DiagnosisProbe:
    def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
        original_mode = self.view.model.training
        self.view.model.eval()
        try:
            with torch.no_grad():
                metrics, definitions = existing_family_aware_probes(train_loader)
                padding = verify_padding_against_unpadded_reference(
                    view=self.view, atol=1e-5, rtol=1e-4,
                    compare_features=True, compare_scores=True,
                    vary_leading_padding=True, vary_batch_companions=True)
                metrics['padding_verification'] = padding
                if not padding['passed']:
                    metrics['temporal_audit'] = {
                        'status': 'unavailable',
                        'reason': 'Resolve padding computation consistently in training and predictor, retrain, then repeat audit.'}
                else:
                    records = []
                    for user, history in deterministic_training_history_subset(limit=200):
                        target = history[-1]
                        context = history[:-1][-baseline_max_length:]
                        if len(context) < 4:
                            record_skip('short_context'); continue
                        negatives = sample_unique_real_items(
                            count=99, exclude=set(history),
                            rng=stable_local_rng(seed=42, user=user))
                        if negatives is None:
                            record_skip('insufficient_negatives'); continue
                        candidates = [target] + negatives
                        prefix, latest = context[:-1], context[-1]
                        k = max(1, len(prefix) // 4)
                        variants = {
                            'original': context,
                            'last_only': [latest],
                            'recent_deleted': prefix[:-k] + [latest],
                            'oldest_deleted': prefix[k:] + [latest]}
                        for repeat in range(5):
                            variants['prefix_shuffle_' + str(repeat)] = (
                                deterministic_shuffle(prefix, seed=42, user=user, repeat=repeat)
                                + [latest])
                        outcomes = {}
                        for name, events in variants.items():
                            sequence = left_pad(events, baseline_max_length)
                            features = self.view.log2feats(sequence)
                            last = greatest_nonzero_input_index(sequence)
                            logits = self.view.predict_score(features[:, last], candidates)
                            outcomes[name] = rank_hit_rr_top10(
                                logits, candidates, target,
                                tie_rule='ascending_item_id')
                        records.append(within_user_paired_effects(
                            outcomes, average_shuffle_repeats=True,
                            exposure=verified_or_unknown_training_exposure(user, target)))
                    metrics['temporal_audit'] = summarize_category_records(records)
                    # The host aggregates category records; the probe need not see other models.
                    # Resample users within every category, retain paired outcomes, then
                    # average four category effects. Use 2,000 replicates, seed 42,
                    # percentile 95% intervals; require all four category summaries.
                definitions.update(padding_and_temporal_definitions_with_limitations())
                return {'metrics': metrics, 'metric_definitions': definitions}
        finally:
            self.view.model.train(original_mode)

# If and only if padding correction is required, implement within the same GRU backbone:
# compact valid input embeddings -> right-padded prefixes -> pack with true lengths
# -> existing GRU -> unpack -> scatter features back to original left-padded positions.
# Handle empty rows separately. Update training and predictor writer, retrain, then audit.

def diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    return evidence_grounded_prompt(
        metrics=raw_diagnosis['metrics'],
        definitions=raw_diagnosis['metric_definitions'],
        require_exposure_and_uncertainty_labels=True,
        prohibit_unobserved_preference_and_causal_claims=True)

originality.positive: Combines padding verification with matched temporal controls that separate latest-item dependence from earlier-context effects in the supplied diagnostic interface.
originality.negative: Padding-correct recurrent execution, sequence ablations and paired ranking comparisons are established techniques; this is a methodological adaptation.

future_potential.positive: Can distinguish implementation artifacts from temporal sensitivity and guide a small, interpretable set of subsequent GRU4Rec training experiments.
future_potential.negative: Inference perturbations can be outside the training distribution, and in-sample targets cannot demonstrate improved unseen-interaction recommendations.

code_difficulty.positive: The audit reuses existing histories, scoring hooks and a single trained checkpoint without requiring a new model family.
code_difficulty.negative: Reproducible padding verification, feature-layout preservation, paired controls and category-level aggregation require more work than the original rating of three suggested.

related_work.title: Does It Look Sequential? (2024)
contributions: Investigates sequential recommendation through inference-history shuffling with fixed trained models.
Motivates measuring ranking accuracy and recommendation-list stability separately.
limitations: Its shuffling can change the latest input item, so it does not independently isolate earlier-order dependence.
Perturbation sensitivity does not establish causal intent or guarantee improvement from recency-aware training.

related_work.title: Hidasi and Czapp: Recommendation Evaluation Flaws (2023)
contributions: Documents disagreements between sampled-negative and full-catalog evaluation.
limitations: Does not identify which training intervention improves the pinned four-category objective.
Supplementary catalog diagnostics cannot replace the mandated sampled validation selection metric.

related_work.title: FActScore: Fine-grained Atomic Evaluation of Factual Precision in Long Form Text Generation (2023)
contributions: Decomposes generated statements into atomic claims and evaluates source support.
Motivates separating measured model behavior from unsupported preference explanations.
limitations: Does not validate recovery of user preferences or rejection reasons from implicit histories.

related_work.title: PyTorch GRU Documentation
contributions: Specifies recurrent gate equations showing that zero inputs can still update hidden states through recurrent transformations and biases.
limitations: Documents GRU behavior but does not establish whether the supplied baseline already handles padding correctly.

related_work.title: PyTorch Embedding Documentation
contributions: Explains padding_idx behavior and the default zero padding embedding.
limitations: A fixed padding embedding does not prevent downstream recurrent state updates.

related_work.title: PyTorch pack_padded_sequence Documentation
contributions: Provides packed execution using valid sequence-prefix lengths.
Supports a padding-invariant GRU implementation after compacting left-padded histories.
limitations: Direct packing of left-padded inputs would retain leading padding and discard valid trailing events.
Compaction requires restoring the external per-position feature layout and separately handling empty histories.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Analyzes why sampled ranking metrics need not preserve full-catalog model comparisons.
limitations: Does not eliminate candidate-sampling uncertainty or prescribe a better intervention for this task.

related_work.title: Statistical Significance Tests for Machine Translation Evaluation (2004)
contributions: Provides a reference for paired bootstrap resampling, adapted here to paired user outcomes within category.
limitations: The recommendation-specific user clustering and four-category macro aggregation are proposed adaptations.
User bootstrap intervals do not capture training randomness, candidate resampling or repeated-search bias.
